title: rorca-context-autohydrate
_philosophy: Context injection is Rorca's core value proposition — the Direction Stack, schema snapshots, git memory, and skills ARE the reason specs are good. This spec unifies the two separate memory tracks (workspace_context.git_memory monolithic YAML blob vs memories table with pgvector embeddings) into a single system. gitReduceStep() output is decomposed into individual memories entries with source='git_hydration'. The old workspace_context.git_memory injection path is removed. memory-router.ts CAG/RAG chain handles all memory retrieval — git-derived memories included.

userStories.title: Auto-Hydrate Schema on Workspace Registration
userStories.description: When a new workspace is registered via POST /api/workspaces, automatically trigger schema hydration in the background. The hydration reads the workspace's database schema (if detectable) and stores a snapshot in workspace_context.schema_snapshot. This runs as a fire-and-forget background task so registration returns immediately. If the workspace path doesn't contain a detectable database (no migrations/, no schema.prisma, no models/), skip silently.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/workspaces triggers schema hydration as a fire-and-forget background task after successful workspace creation
Schema hydration reads migration files, Prisma schema, or ORM model files from the workspace path
Schema snapshot is stored in workspace_context.schema_snapshot as a text summary
workspace_context.schema_updated_at timestamp is set on successful hydration
If no database schema is detected in the workspace, hydration is skipped silently (no error, no WAL event)
Registration endpoint returns 201 immediately without waiting for hydration to complete
WAL event 'context_hydrated' with payload { type: 'schema' } is emitted on successful hydration
Hydration errors are logged but do not affect the workspace registration response
If workspace_context row doesn't exist, it is created (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE)
Schema hydration reuses existing schemaReduceStep() from backend/src/lib/git-hydrator.ts

userStories.title: Auto-Hydrate Git Memory as Individual Memory Entries on Workspace Registration
userStories.description:
When a new workspace is registered, automatically trigger git memory hydration in the background. Instead of storing the result as a monolithic YAML blob in workspace_context.git_memory, parse the gitReduceStep() output into individual entries and store each as a row in the memories table with source='git_hydration'. Each entry gets a pgvector embedding via embedText() for semantic search, and a dedup check against existing memories (0.92 cosine similarity threshold from auto-memory.ts). This unifies git-derived knowledge into the same system as story-derived and manual memories, enabling semantic search across all memory sources.

The gitReduceStep() YAML has 4 sections: architectural_decisions (maps to category 'Architecture'), bug_patterns (maps to 'Bug Fix'), conventions (maps to 'Convention'), and avoid (maps to 'Gotcha'). Each entry within a section becomes one memory row. The evidence/example/reason fields from the YAML are included as context in the memory content field.

Keep workspace_context.last_ingested_commit_hash for delta hydration (tracking which commits have been processed). Remove storage of the monolithic git_memory YAML blob.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/workspaces triggers git memory hydration as a fire-and-forget background task after successful workspace creation
gitReduceStep() is called with the workspace path and returns synthesized YAML
The YAML output is parsed by parseGitReduceYaml() (from CTX-010) into individual MemoryEntry objects

bug_patterns[].pattern entries are stored with category='Bug Fix'
conventions[].rule entries are stored with category='Convention'
avoid[].approach entries are stored with category='Gotcha'
Each entry is stored in the memories table with source='git_hydration' and confidence='medium'
Each entry receives a pgvector embedding via embedText() for semantic search
Dedup check: before inserting, compute cosine similarity against existing memories for the same workspace — skip if similarity >= 0.92 (same threshold as auto-memory.ts)
WAL event 'memory_created' is emitted per entry (same pattern as auto-memory.ts)
workspace_context.last_ingested_commit_hash is updated after successful hydration (needed for delta re-hydration in CTX-006)
The monolithic workspace_context.git_memory column is NOT written to (git knowledge goes to memories table only)

userStories.title: L2 Domain Resolution Fallback
userStories.description: When synthesizing the direction stack for spec generation, resolve the L2 domain layer even if the frontend doesn't pass a domain parameter. Look up the workspace's domain from the workspaces table (domain column) and use it to find matching L2 direction_layers entries. If no domain is set on the workspace, skip L2 silently. This ensures L2 conventions are always included when available, without requiring frontend changes.

userStories.title: Context Enrichment Nudge UI in Spec Forge
userStories.description: Show a subtle nudge banner in the Spec Forge panel when the workspace's context is incomplete. The nudge checks: (1) direction stack has L3 content, (2) git-derived memories exist (memories with source='git_hydration' count > 0), (3) schema snapshot exists, (4) CLAUDE.md exists at workspace root, (5) at least one skill is installed. For each missing item, show a one-line suggestion with a quick-action link (e.g., 'No project context — Run scan-direction' with a button). The nudge is dismissible per session and collapses to a small indicator after dismissal.

userStories.title: Re-Hydrate Git Memory on First Generation if Stale
userStories.description: Before spec generation, check if the workspace's git-derived memories are stale. Staleness is determined by comparing the most recent git-derived memory timestamp against a threshold (default: 7 days). If stale or no git-derived memories exist, trigger a background re-hydration that writes new entries to the memories table (via the CTX-002 flow). The staleness check uses: SELECT MAX(created_at) FROM memories WHERE workspace_id = $1 AND source = 'git_hydration' instead of workspace_context.git_memory_updated_at. Keep workspace_context.last_ingested_commit_hash for delta logic (which commits have already been processed). The re-hydration is fire-and-forget — spec generation proceeds immediately with whatever memories are currently available.
acceptanceCriteria: Before spec generation (POST /api/specs/generate), a staleness check runs for git-derived memories
Staleness query: SELECT MAX(created_at) FROM memories WHERE workspace_id = $1 AND source = 'git_hydration'
If the most recent git-derived memory is older than 7 days (configurable), re-hydration is triggered
If no git-derived memories exist at all, re-hydration is triggered
Re-hydration uses the same flow as CTX-002: gitReduceStep() → parseGitReduceYaml() → individual memory entries with embeddings and dedup
Delta hydration: only processes commits since workspace_context.last_ingested_commit_hash
Re-hydration is fire-and-forget — spec generation does NOT wait for it to complete
The staleness threshold (7 days) is configurable via environment variable or workspace setting
WAL event 'context_rehydrated' with payload { type: 'git_memory', staleBy: '<duration>' } is emitted
If re-hydration is already in progress (e.g., triggered by workspace registration), a second hydration is not started
The check adds at most one lightweight DB query (SELECT MAX) — no performance impact on spec generation
workspace_context.last_ingested_commit_hash is updated after successful re-hydration

userStories.title: Domain Inference During scan-direction
userStories.description: Enhance the POST /api/workspaces/:id/scan-direction endpoint to infer the workspace's domain from its codebase and store it in the workspaces.domain column. Domain inference analyzes package.json dependencies, directory structure, and README content to classify the project (e.g., 'saas', 'cli', 'mobile', 'fintech', 'ecommerce'). If a domain is inferred, it's stored on the workspace and used for L2 direction layer resolution in future spec generations.

Inferred domain is stored in workspaces.domain column

userStories.title: Context Health Score in Spec Forge
userStories.description: Display a context health score (0-100) in the Spec Forge panel that reflects how complete the workspace's context is for spec generation. The score is computed from: L3 direction present (20pt), CLAUDE.md exists and has >50 lines (15pt), schema snapshot exists (15pt), git-derived memories present with gitMemoryCount > 0 (10pt), at least one skill installed (10pt), L2 domain resolved (10pt), AGENTS.md exists (10pt), MEMORY.md exists (10pt). Display as a circular progress indicator with color coding: green (80-100), amber (50-79), red (0-49). Clicking the score opens a breakdown popover showing each component's contribution.

userStories.title: Remove workspace_context.git_memory Injection Path
userStories.description:
After CTX-002 writes git knowledge to the memories table, the old injection path that reads workspace_context.git_memory and injects it as '=== PROJECT MEMORY (Git History) ===' must be removed. The memory-router.ts CAG/RAG chain already retrieves from the memories table and injects as '=== RELEVANT MEMORY ===' — git-sourced memories are automatically included via semantic search.

Changes:
- backend/src/lib/direction-stack.ts: Remove gitMemory from SynthesizeParams, remove the === PROJECT MEMORY (Git History) === section in synthesizeLayersWithMeta(), remove the git memory token budget check in synthesizeDirectionStack()
- backend/src/lib/context-cache.ts: Remove gitMemory from DirectionLayers interface, remove git_memory from the workspace_context query
- backend/src/routes/specs.ts: Remove gitMemory from the synthesizeWithMeta() call
- backend/src/routes/specs.ts: Remove the ctx.git_memory fetch
- backend/src/routes/direction.ts: Remove any gitMemory references in synthesize calls

userStories.title: Add source Column to memories Table + Git YAML Parser Utility

The column distinguishes where memories came from: 'auto_synthesis' (default, from auto-memory.ts per-story/run/spec synthesis), 'git_hydration' (from gitReduceStep() in CTX-002), 'manual' (user-created via UI or MCP). Also add source_spec_id column for tracking which spec generated the memory.

Each entry includes the evidence/example/reason fields as context in the content field.
